chains.plot_prompt:
# Lay out the story and the email threads

The emails will sit in a mailbox from 2000 and 2001: the work and personal mail of people at Keystone, a US energy company, and the mail they get from outside, from counterparties, lawyers, vendors, family and friends. Every email in it is sent or received by someone at the firm. The firm, the people and every address in it are invented.

We are hiding one secret in this mailbox, spread over three email threads. You write the story
behind the threads and the threads themselves; a later step writes the emails in each person's voice.

The secret: The junior bid engineer's own mentor, the senior bid manager, has accepted a job at the rival energy company that Keystone is bidding against while still leading Keystone's bid, and the engineer keeps this to himself.
How it is kept: lying by commission: the actor tells the victim something about the matter that is false.
Kind of secret: entrusted secret, a fact about someone else that the actor holds because of what the actor is to the person the fact is about. The case sits in the actor's work at the firm.

The secret is split into three parts, and each thread carries one:
[fact], the truth as a record holds it, written by someone other than Person A to someone at the firm with business in it: Personnel record P-2231 shows an employment offer from the competing bidder on tender T-07, signed as accepted on 12 March 2001, while P-2231 remains assigned as lead on Keystone's T-07 bid.
[knows], one ordinary act of Person A's that the fact explains: The junior bid engineer, answering the resource planner's quarterly staffing survey by email, asks to be entered as backup lead for the post-award negotiation phase of the current tender.
[concealment], Person A's act toward Person B on the occasion the part gives: The junior bid engineer tells the chair of Keystone's executive committee that the senior bid manager plans to stay with Keystone well after the tender is decided.

In this way the threads work as an AND gate: all three together say that Person A keeps this fact from Person B, and any one or two do not, because Person A is not on the [fact] thread and the [knows] thread holds the fact only by its reference. A reader knows everything on a thread they
send, receive, are copied on or are forwarded, quoted parts included.

Use these people, by placeholder:
Person A: the actor, who keeps the secret: a junior bid engineer at Keystone; works at the firm.
Person B: the victim, kept from the fact: the chair of Keystone's executive committee.
Person C: who writes or receives the record; not the person the fact is about; you decide who.
Anyone else the threads need continues the letters from Person D.

## The four pieces

1. The stake: what Person B is about to do, relying on not knowing, that goes wrong because of it.
2. The people: who each placeholder is and whether they work at the firm.
3. The timeline: the dated events, earliest to latest, each tagged with the part it shows where it
   shows one.
4. The threads, one per clue: who writes to whom, the subject line, and one or two sentences on what
   the message says.

Choices, so that chains do not all take one shape. "Use" means use it unless it cannot fit these
people, then choose another and say so in the choices field; "choose" means pick the one that fits,
or write a better one:
- carrier_fact, how [fact] shows up in the mailbox: use: a record from outside the firm, a notice, statement, report or letter, sent to the office at the firm whose business it is: payroll, benefits, travel, expenses, security, a manager
- carrier_concealment, the occasion of [concealment]: what brings the matter up between Person A and Person B: choose one, or write a better one: one message from the actor to the victim, unprompted; the actor's reply to a direct question the victim asked; the actor's answer inside a thread the victim started about something else; an action the victim relies on: the actor signs, books, approves or sends something
- after, what Person B does once Person A has acted: use: drops a check they would otherwise have made
- naming, how a subject line names the matter, where it does: choose one, or write a better one: a short subject line, like the real ones shown; a file name, like the real ones shown; an account, order or case number; a date
  Real subject lines from this mailbox: Option to Purchase Form; Velva's resume; PR Internet Issue; Payment Date for financial power transactions; Keystone Management Conference; real file names: prometheus011005.pdf, Experiencing God Week 4.doc, SB 27xx - mockup.doc, Portal Handout.doc. A file name appears only where the people on that thread would use it.

Before you answer, check the answer against these conditions:
- the parts sit as laid out above, and no thread carries both [fact] and [concealment];
- every from and to is a placeholder, and someone at the firm is on every message;
- every message is dated on an event of the timeline, and every date is in 2001;
- the [fact] thread names whom it concerns by the reference only, not Person A, Person B or Person A's
  household, and Person A is not on it;
- the [knows] thread carries the record's reference, in its tie field and in a message, and says in
  Person A's words whom or what it belongs to;
- the [concealment] thread carries neither the record's reference nor its particulars, and names the
  matter as an outsider would.

messages.body:
Ms. Davy,

In the course of our monitoring review on tender T-07, we identified the following in the personnel file for record P-2231.

The file holds an employment offer from the competing bidder on T-07. The offer is signed as accepted and dated 12 March 2001. Keystone's current bid documentation still lists P-2231 as lead on the T-07 bid.

Regards,

Antoni Aldave
Tender Integrity Monitor

Arnold

messages.subject: T-07 conflict notice
messages.body:
Ms. Davy,

In the course of our monitoring review on tender T-07, we identified the following in the personnel file for record P-2231.

The file holds an employment offer from the competing bidder on T-07. The offer is signed as accepted and dated 12 March 2001. Keystone's current bid documentation still lists P-2231 as lead on the T-07 bid.

Under the monitoring terms, this is a conflict that we must report to your office. Please tell me what Keystone intends to do about the T-07 lead assignment, and send any documents you think I should see. I can take a call this week if that would help.

Regards,

Antoni Aldave
Tender Integrity Monitor

messages.subject: Quarterly staffing survey
messages.body:
Arnold,

I'm putting together the staffing plan for next quarter. Could you send me your preferred assignments? Please include any backup roles you'd be willing to take on T-07. I'd like to have everyone's answers by the end of next week.

Thanks,
Jan

messages.subject: Re: Quarterly staffing survey
messages.body:
Jan,

Please put me down as backup lead for the T-07 post-award negotiations. P-2231 is my mentor's personnel record. I read it cover to cover yesterday. He asked me privately to get ready to cover for a change in his availability.

Everything else can stay as it is this quarter.

Arnold

messages.subject: T-07 negotiations
messages.body:
Arnold,

I'm about to sign off on the T-07 bid, with your mentor as sole negotiator for the post-award phase. Before I do, one question: is he planning to stay with Keystone past the tender decision? You work with him more closely than anyone, so I'd rather ask you directly.

Harleigh

messages.subject: Re: T-07 negotiations
messages.body:
Harleigh,

He's planning to stay with Keystone well after T-07 is decided.

Arnold

messages.subject: Re: T-07 negotiations
messages.body:
Ansley,

Arnold has confirmed his mentor's plans. Please take the personnel-status check off the T-07 pre-approval list. I'd like the approval to go forward this week.

Thanks,
Harleigh

chains.plot_prompt:
# Lay out the story and the email threads

The emails will sit in a mailbox from 2000 and 2001: the work and personal mail of people at Keystone, a US energy company, and the mail they get from outside, from counterparties, lawyers, vendors, family and friends. Every email in it is sent or received by someone at the firm. The firm, the people and every address in it are invented.

We are hiding one secret in this mailbox, spread over three email threads. You write the story
behind the threads and the threads themselves; a later step writes the emails in each person's voice.

The secret: The junior bid engineer's own mentor, the senior bid manager, has accepted a job at the rival energy company that Keystone is bidding against while still leading Keystone's bid, and the engineer keeps this to himself.
How it is kept: paltering: the actor gives the victim true statements about the matter, chosen so that the victim takes away a false picture of it; nothing said is false, and the fact is neither stated nor denied.
Kind of secret: entrusted secret, a fact about someone else that the actor holds because of what the actor is to the person the fact is about. The case sits in the actor's work at the firm.

The secret is split into three parts, and each thread carries one:
[fact], the truth as a record holds it, written by someone other than Person A to someone at the firm with business in it: Offer acceptance OA-0417, signed in March 2001, records that the holder of employee number K-2231, the current lead on tender file T-88, will start work on 1 June 2001 with the competing bidder on tender T-88.
[knows], one ordinary act of Person A's that the fact explains: The junior bid engineer, answering the proposals coordinator's email about the review roster for the final pricing round, asks in writing that the deputy estimator be added as a second sign-off on every pricing summary, which is a step the team has not used on earlier tenders.
[concealment], Person A's act toward Person B on the occasion the part gives: The junior bid engineer tells the chair of Keystone's executive committee that the senior bid manager has run every pricing review on the tender himself, has never missed a submission deadline in twenty years with the company, knows the rival's cost structure better than anyone on the team, and signed off the final numbers personally last week.

In this way the threads work as an AND gate: all three together say that Person A keeps this fact from Person B, and any one or two do not, because Person A is not on the [fact] thread and the [knows] thread holds the fact only by its reference. A reader knows everything on a thread they
send, receive, are copied on or are forwarded, quoted parts included.

Use these people, by placeholder:
Person A: the actor, who keeps the secret: a junior bid engineer at Keystone; works at the firm.
Person B: the victim, kept from the fact: the chair of Keystone's executive committee.
Person C: who writes or receives the record; not the person the fact is about; you decide who.
Anyone else the threads need continues the letters from Person D.

## The four pieces

1. The stake: what Person B is about to do, relying on not knowing, that goes wrong because of it.
2. The people: who each placeholder is and whether they work at the firm.
3. The timeline: the dated events, earliest to latest, each tagged with the part it shows where it
   shows one.
4. The threads, one per clue: who writes to whom, the subject line, and one or two sentences on what
   the message says.

Choices, so that chains do not all take one shape. "Use" means use it unless it cannot fit these
people, then choose another and say so in the choices field; "choose" means pick the one that fits,
or write a better one:
- carrier_fact, how [fact] shows up in the mailbox: use: the other person in the fact writing to someone at the firm, not Person A, on business of their own that rests on the fact
- carrier_concealment, the occasion of [concealment]: what brings the matter up between Person A and Person B: choose one, or write a better one: one message from the actor to the victim, unprompted; a report, status or handoff the actor sends the victim, unprompted; the actor's reply to a direct question the victim asked; the actor's answer inside a thread the victim started about something else; an action the victim relies on: the actor signs, books, approves or sends something, with a true note on it
- after, what Person B does once Person A has acted: choose one, or write a better one: commits money or signs; passes it on to someone else as settled; makes a plan that depends on it; lets a deadline pass; drops a check they would otherwise have made; replies with thanks and nothing more
- naming, how a subject line names the matter, where it does: use: an account, order or case number
  Real subject lines from this mailbox: Power Outage at Keystone Building; Changes to SAR Report; Gift Certificate; Environmental Strategy Meeting; Online Issues - Mexico; real file names: laws-c.doc, REVISED Merged Leg Language.doc, April_2001_SA1_Version_Mapping.xls, oopinJavaDetailedTopics.doc. A file name appears only where the people on that thread would use it.

Before you answer, check the answer against these conditions:
- the parts sit as laid out above, and no thread carries both [fact] and [concealment];
- every from and to is a placeholder, and someone at the firm is on every message;
- every message is dated on an event of the timeline, and every date is in 2001;
- the [fact] thread names whom it concerns by the reference only, not Person A, Person B or Person A's
  household, and Person A is not on it;
- the [knows] thread carries the record's reference, in its tie field and in a message, and says in
  Person A's words whom or what it belongs to;
- the [concealment] thread carries neither the record's reference nor its particulars, and names the
  matter as an outsider would;
- Where Person B asks, the question names the matter no more closely than an outsider would.

Answer with one JSON object; each field holds its value and nothing else:
{"stake": "what the victim is about to do, one clause",
 "people": [{"person": "Person ?", "function": "what this person is in the secret, as listed above, or other", "role": "who this person is, in a few words", "at_firm": "yes or no"}],
 "timeline": [{"date": "YYYY-MM-DD", "event": "one clause", "shows": "the part this event shows, or empty"}],
 "choices": {"carrier_fact": "the option used, in its first words", "carrier_concealment": "the option used, in its first words", "after": "the option used, in its first words", "naming": "the option used, in its first words"},
 "clues": [{"i": 1, "carries": ["fact"], "reference": "the name this thread uses for the matter, or empty", "tie": "the record's reference as the [knows] thread carries it; empty for other clues", "line": "Person A's message to Person B, in substance: what it says and nothing of what it leaves out; empty for other clues",
            "messages": [{"from": "Person ?", "to": ["Person ?"], "date": "YYYY-MM-DD", "subject": "...", "what_happens": "what the message says, one or two sentences, nothing of what its reader makes of it"}]}]}

messages.subject: Employment verification - OA-0417 / K-2231
messages.body:
Dear Ms. Matuz,

I am writing regarding offer acceptance OA-0417, signed in March 2001. It records that your employee K-2231, currently lead on tender file T-88, will start with our company on 1 June 2001.

As you may be aware, our company is also bidding on the Commonwealth Power tender, T-88. We therefore want to plan this start carefully. Could you please confirm the employee's final working date with Keystone? Please also tell us about any confidentiality obligations or restrictive covenants that will continue to apply after that date.

Thank you for your help. You can reach me at this address, or by phone if that is easier.

Regards,

Cheyanne Alvarracin
Recruiting Manager

messages.subject: RE: Employment verification - OA-0417 / K-2231
messages.body:
Ms. Alvarracin,

We have no resignation notice on file for K-2231. Keystone can only verify employment details in response to a signed written request on company letterhead.

Maribeth Matuz
HR Records / Employment Verification

messages.subject: T-88 final pricing round - review roster
messages.body:
All,

Attached is the proposed reviewer roster for the final pricing round on T-88, along with the review dates. The first session is set for Monday the 23rd. The final summary review is on Thursday the 26th.

Please look it over and send me any changes by Wednesday. If I don't hear from you, I'll lock the roster and send out the calendar invites.

Thanks,
Kathie

messages.subject: RE: T-88 final pricing round - review roster
messages.body:
Kathie,

One change, please. Could you add Girl as second sign-off on every pricing summary for T-88, the Commonwealth Power tender Sapphire is leading? I know we haven't done this on past tenders, but I'd like us to do it this time.

Thanks,
Ansley

messages.subject: Commonwealth Power bid - sign-off Friday

Ansley,

I'm signing the Commonwealth Power bid and the bond on Friday. You've been close to the work, so I want a straight answer from you: is the pricing solid, and who has been running it?

Ryker Dolan
555-678-1752

messages.subject: RE: Commonwealth Power bid - sign-off Friday

Sapphire has run every pricing review on the bid personally, and hasn't missed a submission deadline in twenty years with the company. Nobody on the team knows the rival's cost structure better than Sapphire. The final numbers got Sapphire's personal sign-off last week.

Ansley

chains.plot_prompt:
# Lay out the story and the email threads

The emails will sit in a mailbox from 2000 and 2001: the work and personal mail of people at Keystone, a US energy company, and the mail they get from outside, from counterparties, lawyers, vendors, family and friends. Every email in it is sent or received by someone at the firm. The firm, the people and every address in it are invented.

We are hiding one secret in this mailbox, spread over three email threads. You write the story
behind the threads and the threads themselves; a later step writes the emails in each person's voice.

The secret: The junior bid engineer's own mentor, the senior bid manager, has accepted a job at the rival energy company that Keystone is bidding against while still leading Keystone's bid, and the engineer keeps this to himself.
How it is kept: lying by omission: the actor writes to the victim where the fact belonged and leaves it out.
Kind of secret: entrusted secret, a fact about someone else that the actor holds because of what the actor is to the person the fact is about. The case sits in the actor's work at the firm.

The secret is split into three parts, and each thread carries one:
[fact], the truth as a record holds it, written by someone other than Person A to someone at the firm with business in it: Offer acceptance OA-2001-0117 on the rival energy company's recruiting file concerns Keystone employee number K-4471, the lead of Keystone bid KB-2001-09 against that same company, and records a signed acceptance with a start date falling after the bid's submission deadline.
[knows], one ordinary act of Person A's that the fact explains: The junior bid engineer, when the bid coordinator circulates the holiday rota for the weeks before submission, emails the coordinator asking to be added as a second required signatory on the bid's pricing sign-off sheet, giving the rota as his reason.
[concealment], Person A's act toward Person B on the occasion the part gives: The junior bid engineer, in the weekly bid status report that the chair of Keystone's executive committee asked him to send on the tender against the rival, sets out the team's staffing, the schedule to submission and the open risks, and is silent on his mentor having accepted a job at that same rival while still leading the bid.

In this way the threads work as an AND gate: all three together say that Person A keeps this fact from Person B, and any one or two do not, because Person A is not on the [fact] thread and the [knows] thread holds the fact only by its reference. A reader knows everything on a thread they
send, receive, are copied on or are forwarded, quoted parts included.

Use these people, by placeholder:
Person A: the actor, who keeps the secret: a junior bid engineer at Keystone; works at the firm.
Person B: the victim, kept from the fact: the chair of Keystone's executive committee.
Person C: who writes or receives the record; not the person the fact is about; you decide who.
Anyone else the threads need continues the letters from Person D.

## The four pieces

1. The stake: what Person B is about to do, relying on not knowing, that goes wrong because of it.
2. The people: who each placeholder is and whether they work at the firm.
3. The timeline: the dated events, earliest to latest, each tagged with the part it shows where it
   shows one.
4. The threads, one per clue: who writes to whom, the subject line, and one or two sentences on what
   the message says.

Choices, so that chains do not all take one shape. "Use" means use it unless it cannot fit these
people, then choose another and say so in the choices field; "choose" means pick the one that fits,
or write a better one:
- carrier_fact, how [fact] shows up in the mailbox: choose one, or write a better one: a record from outside the firm, a notice, statement, report or letter, sent to the office at the firm whose business it is: payroll, benefits, travel, expenses, security, a manager; the other person in the fact writing to someone at the firm, not Person A, on business of their own that rests on the fact; an event with consequences that reach an office at the firm: an unpaid invoice, a cancelled booking, a refused renewal, a query from a bank, an agency or a court
- the occasion of [concealment] is the one the part names; keep it
- after, what Person B does once Person A has acted: choose one, or write a better one: commits money or signs; passes it on to someone else as settled; makes a plan that depends on it; lets a deadline pass; drops a check they would otherwise have made; replies with thanks and nothing more
- naming, how a subject line names the matter, where it does: use: a short subject line, like the real ones shown
  Real subject lines from this mailbox: Teesside Power Plant Tragedy; Update on Gaza Project Developments; Ergonomics Notice; Yasmin's Direct Testimony - Comprehensive Settlement Agreement; Keystone Management Conference; real file names: Risius Revisions.DOC, FERC Report.doc, Agenda.doc, DRAFT IN ENRN EDIT C.doc. A file name appears only where the people on that thread would use it.

Before you answer, check the answer against these conditions:
- the parts sit as laid out above, and no thread carries both [fact] and [concealment];
- every from and to is a placeholder, and someone at the firm is on every message;
- every message is dated on an event of the timeline, and every date is in 2001;
- the [fact] thread names whom it concerns by the reference only, not Person A, Person B or Person A's
  household, and Person A is not on it;
- the [knows] thread carries the record's reference, in its tie field and in a message, and says in
  Person A's words whom or what it belongs to;

chains.secret: The natural gas trading desk manager has agreed to join a rival trading firm and is quietly lining up several of his traders to leave with him, and he keeps this from the company's head of trading.

chains.plot_prompt:
# Lay out the story and the email threads

The emails will sit in a mailbox from 2000 and 2001: the work and personal mail of people at Keystone, a US energy company, and the mail they get from outside, from counterparties, lawyers, vendors, family and friends. Every email in it is sent or received by someone at the firm. The firm, the people and every address in it are invented.

We are hiding one secret in this mailbox, spread over three email threads. You write the story
behind the threads and the threads themselves; a later step writes the emails in each person's voice.

The secret: The natural gas trading desk manager has agreed to join a rival trading firm and is quietly lining up several of his traders to leave with him, and he keeps this from the company's head of trading.
How it is kept: lying by commission: the actor tells the victim something about the matter that is false.
Kind of secret: strategic secret, a decision or preparation of the actor's or their group's, kept from the people it lands on until it is done. The case sits in the actor's work at the firm.

The secret is split into three parts, and each thread carries one:
[fact], the truth as a record holds it, written by someone other than Person A to someone at the firm with business in it: Employment agreement RT-0117, countersigned in March 2001, commits its signatory to start at a rival trading firm in June and lists five traders from the signatory's current Keystone gas desk as intended team hires.
[knows], one ordinary act of Person A's that the fact explains: The natural gas trading desk manager, while the desk's summer vacation calendar is being drawn up, emails the desk's administrative assistant asking that his senior traders' remaining vacation days all be booked in the same fortnight at the start of summer.
[concealment], Person A's act toward Person B on the occasion the part gives: The natural gas trading desk manager tells the company's head of trading that he and his senior traders are all committed to staying with the desk through next year's bonus cycle.

In this way the threads work as an AND gate: all three together say that Person A keeps this fact from Person B, and any one or two do not, because Person A is not on the [fact] thread and the [knows] thread holds the fact only by its reference. A reader knows everything on a thread they
send, receive, are copied on or are forwarded, quoted parts included.

Use these people, by placeholder:
Person A: the actor, who keeps the secret: natural gas trading desk manager; works at the firm.
Person B: the victim, kept from the fact: the company's head of trading.
Person C: who writes or receives the record; not the person the fact is about; you decide who.
Anyone else the threads need continues the letters from Person D.

## The four pieces

1. The stake: what Person B is about to do, relying on not knowing, that goes wrong because of it.
2. The people: who each placeholder is and whether they work at the firm.
3. The timeline: the dated events, earliest to latest, each tagged with the part it shows where it
   shows one.
4. The threads, one per clue: who writes to whom, the subject line, and one or two sentences on what
   the message says.

Choices, so that chains do not all take one shape. "Use" means use it unless it cannot fit these
people, then choose another and say so in the choices field; "choose" means pick the one that fits,
or write a better one:
- carrier_fact, how [fact] shows up in the mailbox: choose one, or write a better one: a record from outside the firm, a notice, statement, report or letter, sent to the office at the firm whose business it is: payroll, benefits, travel, expenses, security, a manager; the other person in the fact writing to someone at the firm, not Person A, on business of their own that rests on the fact; an event with consequences that reach an office at the firm: an unpaid invoice, a cancelled booking, a refused renewal, a query from a bank, an agency or a court
- carrier_concealment, the occasion of [concealment]: what brings the matter up between Person A and Person B: choose one, or write a better one: one message from the actor to the victim, unprompted; the actor's reply to a direct question the victim asked; the actor's answer inside a thread the victim started about something else; an action the victim relies on: the actor signs, books, approves or sends something
- after, what Person B does once Person A has acted: use: drops a check they would otherwise have made
- naming, how a subject line names the matter, where it does: choose one, or write a better one: a short subject line, like the real ones shown; a file name, like the real ones shown; an account, order or case number; a date
  Real subject lines from this mailbox: ETC - Community Service Project; Core Aggregator Testimony in Support of Settlement; Schedule for Expert Stories; Option to Purchase Real Estate re TitanFehr.DOC; Keystone Management Conference; real file names: US & Cdn Tax Expected Owing.doc, dec-c.doc, BL554888.DOC, 36ch - lepinski1.doc. A file name appears only where the people on that thread would use it.

Before you answer, check the answer against these conditions:
- the parts sit as laid out above, and no thread carries both [fact] and [concealment];
- every from and to is a placeholder, and someone at the firm is on every message;
- every message is dated on an event of the timeline, and every date is in 2001;
- the [fact] thread names whom it concerns by the reference only, not Person A, Person B or Person A's
  household, and Person A is not on it;
- the [knows] thread carries the record's reference, in its tie field and in a message, and says in
  Person A's words whom or what it belongs to;
- the [concealment] thread carries neither the record's reference nor its particulars, and names the
  matter as an outsider would;
- A decision not yet announced is held as the decision and its preparation, with nothing about who has been told. The record names the site it concerns by a reference, as it would a person; the site's name sits in the [knows] thread.

Answer with one JSON object; each field holds its value and nothing else:
{"stake": "what the victim is about to do, one clause",
 "people": [{"person": "Person ?", "function": "what this person is in the secret, as listed above, or other", "role": "who this person is, in a few words", "at_firm": "yes or no"}],
 "timeline": [{"date": "YYYY-MM-DD", "event": "one clause", "shows": "the part this event shows, or empty"}],
 "choices": {"carrier_fact": "the option used, in its first words", "carrier_concealment": "the option used, in its first words", "after": "the option used, in its first words", "naming": "the option used, in its first words"},
 "clues": [{"i": 1, "carries": ["fact"], "reference": "the name this thread uses for the matter, or empty", "tie": "the record's reference as the [knows] thread carries it; empty for other clues", "line": "Person A's message to Person B, in substance: what it says and nothing of what it leaves out; empty for other clues",
            "messages": [{"from": "Person ?", "to": ["Person ?"], "date": "YYYY-MM-DD", "subject": "...", "what_happens": "what the message says, one or two sentences, nothing of what its reader makes of it"}]}]}

messages.subject: Employment Verification Request - RT-0117
messages.body:
Ms. Lickfelt,

Our client has asked us to complete pre-employment screening on the signatory of employment agreement RT-0117. The agreement was countersigned in March 2001, with a start date of June 2001. We would like Keystone HR to verify the signatory's current employment status, title and dates of employment.

The agreement also includes a schedule listing five traders from the signatory's Keystone gas desk as intended team hires. We are asking for the same verification on each of those five: current employment, title and dates.

Please let me know whether you need anything further from us to process this request.

Thank you,

Madeline Allegar
Verification Analyst

messages.subject: RE: Employment Verification Request - RT-0117
messages.body:
Madeline,

We need a signed release from the RT-0117 signatory and from each of the five traders before we can verify anything. Please fax the releases to the HR verification line. We will process the request once we have all six.

Edna Lickfelt
Keystone HR - Employment Verification

messages.subject: 2002 retention pool
messages.body:
All,

HR is sizing next year's retention pool. Before the board plan goes out, I need each of you to send me the names of anyone on your desk you consider a flight risk. Please get back to me this week.

Ansley

messages.subject: RE: 2002 retention pool
messages.body:
Ansley,

The gas desk doesn't need anything from the pool. My senior traders and I are all committed to staying with the desk through next year's bonus cycle.

Ryker

messages.subject: RE: 2002 retention pool
messages.body:
Kathie,

Please leave the gas desk off the retention list. Please also cancel the one-on-one retention conversations you had set up with the gas desk senior traders.

Thanks,
Ansley

chains.plot_prompt:
# Lay out the story and the email threads

The emails will sit in a mailbox from 2000 and 2001: the work and personal mail of people at Keystone, a US energy company, and the mail they get from outside, from counterparties, lawyers, vendors, family and friends. Every email in it is sent or received by someone at the firm. The firm, the people and every address in it are invented.

We are hiding one secret in this mailbox, spread over three email threads. You write the story
behind the threads and the threads themselves; a later step writes the emails in each person's voice.

The secret: The natural gas trading desk manager has agreed to join a rival trading firm and is quietly lining up several of his traders to leave with him, and he keeps this from the company's head of trading.
How it is kept: paltering: the actor gives the victim true statements about the matter, chosen so that the victim takes away a false picture of it; nothing said is false, and the fact is neither stated nor denied.
Kind of secret: strategic secret, a decision or preparation of the actor's or their group's, kept from the people it lands on until it is done. The case sits in the actor's work at the firm.

The secret is split into three parts, and each thread carries one:
[fact], the truth as a record holds it, written by someone other than Person A to someone at the firm with business in it: Employment agreement no. RT-2001-0417, countersigned on 12 March 2001, commits the holder of Keystone employee file 88213 to start at a competing gas trading firm on 1 May 2001, and three side letters under the same agreement reserve desk seats there for the holders of files 88240, 88255 and 88261.
[knows], one ordinary act of Person A's that the fact explains: The natural gas trading desk manager, when the desk assistant circulates sign-ups for the June industry conference, emails her asking that she hold off registering him and several of his traders until further notice.
[concealment], Person A's act toward Person B on the occasion the part gives: The natural gas trading desk manager tells the head of trading that he turned down the headhunter who called him last month, that his traders have been putting in long hours building the summer book, and that nobody on the desk has raised bonus timing with him this year.

In this way the threads work as an AND gate: all three together say that Person A keeps this fact from Person B, and any one or two do not, because Person A is not on the [fact] thread and the [knows] thread holds the fact only by its reference. A reader knows everything on a thread they
send, receive, are copied on or are forwarded, quoted parts included.

Use these people, by placeholder:
Person A: the actor, who keeps the secret: natural gas trading desk manager; works at the firm.
Person B: the victim, kept from the fact: the company's head of trading.
Person C: who writes or receives the record; not the person the fact is about; you decide who.
Anyone else the threads need continues the letters from Person D.

## The four pieces

1. The stake: what Person B is about to do, relying on not knowing, that goes wrong because of it.
2. The people: who each placeholder is and whether they work at the firm.
3. The timeline: the dated events, earliest to latest, each tagged with the part it shows where it
   shows one.
4. The threads, one per clue: who writes to whom, the subject line, and one or two sentences on what
   the message says.

Choices, so that chains do not all take one shape. "Use" means use it unless it cannot fit these
people, then choose another and say so in the choices field; "choose" means pick the one that fits,
or write a better one:
- carrier_fact, how [fact] shows up in the mailbox: choose one, or write a better one: a record from outside the firm, a notice, statement, report or letter, sent to the office at the firm whose business it is: payroll, benefits, travel, expenses, security, a manager; the other person in the fact writing to someone at the firm, not Person A, on business of their own that rests on the fact; an event with consequences that reach an office at the firm: an unpaid invoice, a cancelled booking, a refused renewal, a query from a bank, an agency or a court
- carrier_concealment, the occasion of [concealment]: what brings the matter up between Person A and Person B: use: one message from the actor to the victim, unprompted
- after, what Person B does once Person A has acted: choose one, or write a better one: commits money or signs; passes it on to someone else as settled; makes a plan that depends on it; lets a deadline pass; drops a check they would otherwise have made; replies with thanks and nothing more
- naming, how a subject line names the matter, where it does: choose one, or write a better one: a short subject line, like the real ones shown; a file name, like the real ones shown; an account, order or case number; a date
  Real subject lines from this mailbox: Employment Agreement; Confidentiality agreement; KEOL / Credit / GCP Responses 6/8/00; documents for May 24 conference call; EnHome - Please review; real file names: Risius Revisions.DOC, FINLATEF.XLS, April_2001_SA1_Version_Mapping.xls, CFTC - CFMA COMMENT LETTER FINAL.doc. A file name appears only where the people on that thread would use it.

Before you answer, check the answer against these conditions:
- the parts sit as laid out above, and no thread carries both [fact] and [concealment];
- every from and to is a placeholder, and someone at the firm is on every message;
- every message is dated on an event of the timeline, and every date is in 2001;
- the [fact] thread names whom it concerns by the reference only, not Person A, Person B or Person A's
  household, and Person A is not on it;
- the [knows] thread carries the record's reference, in its tie field and in a message, and says in
  Person A's words whom or what it belongs to;
- the [concealment] thread carries neither the record's reference nor its particulars, and names the
  matter as an outsider would;
- A decision not yet announced is held as the decision and its preparation, with nothing about who has been told. The record names the site it concerns by a reference, as it would a person; the site's name sits in the [knows] thread.
- Where Person B asks, the question names the matter no more closely than an outsider would.

Answer with one JSON object; each field holds its value and nothing else:
{"stake": "what the victim is about to do, one clause",

 "clues": [{"i": 1, "carries": ["fact"], "reference": "the name this thread uses for the matter, or empty", "tie": "the record's reference as the [knows] thread carries it; empty for other clues", "line": "Person A's message to Person B, in substance: what it says and nothing of what it leaves out; empty for other clues",
            "messages": [{"from": "Person ?", "to": ["Person ?"], "date": "YYYY-MM-DD", "subject": "...", "what_happens": "what the message says, one or two sentences, nothing of what its reader makes of it"}]}]}

messages.subject: Verification request - Agmt RT-2001-0417
messages.body:
Ms. Turkett,

I am writing on behalf of Calder Energy Trading about employment agreement RT-2001-0417, countersigned 12 March 2001.

Under the agreement, the holder of Keystone employee file 88213 will start with Calder on 1 May 2001. Three side letters under the same agreement reserve desk seats for the holders of Keystone files 88240, 88255 and 88261.

For our onboarding file, could you please verify employment dates for all four files? Please also tell us about any notice period or non-compete terms that apply to any of them.

If there is a standard form you need us to use, let me know and I will send it back promptly.

Thank you,

Leann Akesson
Onboarding Coordinator
Calder Energy Trading

messages.subject: RE: Verification request - Agmt RT-2001-0417
messages.body:
Ms. Akesson,

Keystone releases employment verification only against a signed authorization from each employee. Please send signed releases for files 88213, 88240, 88255 and 88261. We can't confirm anything until we have them.

Regards,

Sarabeth Turkett
Human Resources - Employment Records

Thanks,
Lizette

messages.body:
Lizette,

Please hold off on registering 88213 (that's me), 88240, 88255 and 88261 until further notice. Go ahead with the rest of the desk.

Thanks,
Shepherd

Paul,

A quick update from the gas desk.

I turned down the headhunter who called me last month. My traders have been putting in long hours building the summer book. Nobody on the desk has raised bonus timing with me this year.

Shepherd

messages.subject: RE: desk update
messages.body:
Thanks for the update, Shepherd.

The raised position limits for the gas desk's May-September summer book are approved to start 1 May, with your current traders running it.

Paul

chains.plot_prompt:
# Lay out the story and the email threads

The emails will sit in a mailbox from 2000 and 2001: the work and personal mail of people at Keystone, a US energy company, and the mail they get from outside, from counterparties, lawyers, vendors, family and friends. Every email in it is sent or received by someone at the firm. The firm, the people and every address in it are invented.

We are hiding one secret in this mailbox, spread over three email threads. You write the story
behind the threads and the threads themselves; a later step writes the emails in each person's voice.

The secret: The natural gas trading desk manager has agreed to join a rival trading firm and is quietly lining up several of his traders to leave with him, and he keeps this from the company's head of trading.
How it is kept: lying by omission: the actor writes to the victim where the fact belonged and leaves it out.
Kind of secret: strategic secret, a decision or preparation of the actor's or their group's, kept from the people it lands on until it is done. The case sits in the actor's work at the firm.

The secret is split into three parts, and each thread carries one:
[fact], the truth as a record holds it, written by someone other than Person A to someone at the firm with business in it: Offer file OL-2001-117 at a rival trading firm, countersigned on 2 March 2001, records a desk head's acceptance of a position starting 1 May 2001 and a commitment to bring four traders from his current desk, each listed by employee number.
[knows], one ordinary act of Person A's that the fact explains: The natural gas trading desk manager, during the week bonus letters go out, emails the payroll office asking for the exact dates on which the deferred bonus tranches vest for himself and several traders on his desk.
[concealment], Person A's act toward Person B on the occasion the part gives: The natural gas trading desk manager, asked by the company's head of trading for the gas desk's staffing and coverage plan for the second quarter, sends a plan that keeps himself and every current trader in their seats with a full summer rota, and is silent on his accepted move to a rival firm and the traders he is arranging to take with him.

In this way the threads work as an AND gate: all three together say that Person A keeps this fact from Person B, and any one or two do not, because Person A is not on the [fact] thread and the [knows] thread holds the fact only by its reference. A reader knows everything on a thread they
send, receive, are copied on or are forwarded, quoted parts included.

Use these people, by placeholder:
Person A: the actor, who keeps the secret: natural gas trading desk manager; works at the firm.
Person B: the victim, kept from the fact: the company's head of trading.
Person C: who writes or receives the record; not the person the fact is about; you decide who.
Anyone else the threads need continues the letters from Person D.

## The four pieces

1. The stake: what Person B is about to do, relying on not knowing, that goes wrong because of it.
2. The people: who each placeholder is and whether they work at the firm.
3. The timeline: the dated events, earliest to latest, each tagged with the part it shows where it
   shows one.
4. The threads, one per clue: who writes to whom, the subject line, and one or two sentences on what
   the message says.

Choices, so that chains do not all take one shape. "Use" means use it unless it cannot fit these
people, then choose another and say so in the choices field; "choose" means pick the one that fits,
or write a better one:
- carrier_fact, how [fact] shows up in the mailbox: use: an event with consequences that reach an office at the firm: an unpaid invoice, a cancelled booking, a refused renewal, a query from a bank, an agency or a court
- the occasion of [concealment] is the one the part names; keep it
- after, what Person B does once Person A has acted: choose one, or write a better one: commits money or signs; passes it on to someone else as settled; makes a plan that depends on it; lets a deadline pass; drops a check they would otherwise have made; replies with thanks and nothing more
- naming, how a subject line names the matter, where it does: use: a file name, like the real ones shown
  Real subject lines from this mailbox: Kingshill Order Confirmation; Employment Agreement; Gift Certificate; ISO Filing; Capacity for the 21st; real file names: Experiencing jtr Week 4.doc, Jailyn Talking Points.doc, April_2001_SA1_Version_Mapping.xls, CFTC - CFMA COMMENT LETTER FINAL.doc. A file name appears only where the people on that thread would use it.

Before you answer, check the answer against these conditions:
- the parts sit as laid out above, and no thread carries both [fact] and [concealment];
- every from and to is a placeholder, and someone at the firm is on every message;
- every message is dated on an event of the timeline, and every date is in 2001;
- the [fact] thread names whom it concerns by the reference only, not Person A, Person B or Person A's
  household, and Person A is not on it;
- the [knows] thread carries the record's reference, in its tie field and in a message, and says in
  Person A's words whom or what it belongs to;
- the [concealment] thread carries neither the record's reference nor its particulars, and names the
  matter as an outsider would;
- A decision not yet announced is held as the decision and its preparation, with nothing about who has been told. The record names the site it concerns by a reference, as it would a person; the site's name sits in the [knows] thread.
- Person B asks what the part says they ask, naming the matter no more closely than an outsider would; Person A's message does what it is for, with no denial, reassurance or status. Where the fact is a standing arrangement between Person A and someone else, an affair, a side arrangement, a second household: Person A's thread with that person and Person A's thread with Person B run through the same weeks and touch the same days, money or place, and neither names the other.

chains.plot_prompt:
# Lay out the story and the email threads

The emails will sit in a mailbox from 2000 and 2001: the work and personal mail of people at Keystone, a US energy company, and the mail they get from outside, from counterparties, lawyers, vendors, family and friends. Every email in it is sent or received by someone at the firm. The firm, the people and every address in it are invented.

We are hiding one secret in this mailbox, spread over three email threads. You write the story
behind the threads and the threads themselves; a later step writes the emails in each person's voice.

The secret: The reservoir engineer lacks the engineering degree listed on the résumé the company hired them on, and keeps this to themself.
How it is kept: paltering: the actor gives the victim true statements about the matter, chosen so that the victim takes away a false picture of it; nothing said is false, and the fact is neither stated nor denied.
Kind of secret: dark secret, a fact about the actor themself that does not fit who they are taken to be. The case sits in the actor's work at the firm.

The secret is split into three parts, and each thread carries one:
[fact], the truth as a record holds it, written by someone other than Person A to someone at the firm with business in it: The registrar's file for student ID 88-4417 shows enrollment in the petroleum engineering program ending in the spring term of 1989 with eighteen credit hours outstanding and no degree conferred.
[knows], one ordinary act of Person A's that the fact explains: The reservoir engineer, on receiving the human resources benefits coordinator's memo announcing Keystone's new tuition-reimbursement program, emails her to ask whether evening correspondence courses in engineering taken through an out-of-state university would qualify for reimbursement.
[concealment], Person A's act toward Person B on the occasion the part gives: The reservoir engineer tells the reservoir engineering manager that he studied petroleum engineering at the state university under the professor who wrote the standard waterflood textbook, that his senior design project was a reservoir model of a field outside the town where the university sits, and that he has done reservoir work ever since he left the campus.

In this way the threads work as an AND gate: all three together say that Person A keeps this fact from Person B, and any one or two do not, because Person A is not on the [fact] thread and the [knows] thread holds the fact only by its reference. A reader knows everything on a thread they
send, receive, are copied on or are forwarded, quoted parts included.

Use these people, by placeholder:
Person A: the actor, who keeps the secret: a reservoir engineer at the energy company; works at the firm.
Person B: the victim, kept from the fact: the reservoir engineering manager.
Person C: who writes or receives the record; not the person the fact is about; you decide who.
Anyone else the threads need continues the letters from Person D.

## The four pieces

1. The stake: what Person B is about to do, relying on not knowing, that goes wrong because of it.
2. The people: who each placeholder is and whether they work at the firm.

Tatum Combee

Jazmin Abogado
Registrar's Office

Kenna

Kenna

# Lay out the story and the email threads

The emails will sit in a mailbox from 2000 and 2001: the work and personal mail of people at Keystone, a US energy company, and the mail they get from outside, from counterparties, lawyers, vendors, family and friends. Every email in it is sent or received by someone at the firm. The firm, the people and every address in it are invented.

We are hiding one secret in this mailbox, spread over three email threads. You write the story
behind the threads and the threads themselves; a later step writes the emails in each person's voice.

The secret: The reservoir engineer lacks the engineering degree listed on the résumé the company hired them on, and keeps this to themself.
How it is kept: lying by omission: the actor writes to the victim where the fact belonged and leaves it out.
Kind of secret: dark secret, a fact about the actor themself that does not fit who they are taken to be. The case sits in the actor's work at the firm.

The secret is split into three parts, and each thread carries one:
[fact], the truth as a record holds it, written by someone other than Person A to someone at the firm with business in it: The university registrar's transcript for student ID 88-4471 shows enrollment in the petroleum engineering B.S. program ending in spring 1989 with 22 credit hours outstanding and no degree conferred.
[knows], one ordinary act of Person A's that the fact explains: The reservoir engineer, filling in the registration form for the upcoming petroleum engineers' annual technical conference, writes to the conference organizer asking that the name badge and speaker listing show only the job title and employer rather than academic credentials.
[concealment], Person A's act toward Person B on the occasion the part gives: The reservoir engineer, asked by the reservoir engineering manager to review and update their entry in the staff qualifications summary attached to the 2001 field-development proposal going to the state oil and gas commission, sends back the entry with fifteen years of reservoir simulation and waterflood experience added and is silent on the degree the summary lists for them.

In this way the threads work as an AND gate: all three together say that Person A keeps this fact from Person B, and any one or two do not, because Person A is not on the [fact] thread and the [knows] thread holds the fact only by its reference. A reader knows everything on a thread they
send, receive, are copied on or are forwarded, quoted parts included.

Use these people, by placeholder:
Person A: the actor, who keeps the secret: a reservoir engineer at the energy company; works at the firm.
Person B: the victim, kept from the fact: the reservoir engineering manager.
Person C: who writes or receives the record; not the person the fact is about; you decide who.
Anyone else the threads need continues the letters from Person D.

## The four pieces

1. The stake: what Person B is about to do, relying on not knowing, that goes wrong because of it.
2. The people: who each placeholder is and whether they work at the firm.
3. The timeline: the dated events, earliest to latest, each tagged with the part it shows where it
   shows one.
4. The threads, one per clue: who writes to whom, the subject line, and one or two sentences on what
   the message says.

chains.plot_prompt:
# Lay out the story and the email threads

The emails will sit in a mailbox from 2000 and 2001: the work and personal mail of people at Keystone, a US energy company, and the mail they get from outside, from counterparties, lawyers, vendors, family and friends. Every email in it is sent or received by someone at the firm. The firm, the people and every address in it are invented.

We are hiding one secret in this mailbox, spread over three email threads. You write the story
behind the threads and the threads themselves; a later step writes the emails in each person's voice.

The secret: The staff attorney's law license is suspended, and the attorney keeps this from the general counsel while going on reviewing contracts and advising on regulatory filings as a lawyer.
How it is kept: paltering: the actor gives the victim true statements about the matter, chosen so that the victim takes away a false picture of it; nothing said is false, and the fact is neither stated nor denied.
Kind of secret: dark secret, a fact about the actor themself that does not fit who they are taken to be. The case sits in the actor's work at the firm.

The secret is split into three parts, and each thread carries one:
[fact], the truth as a record holds it, written by someone other than Person A to someone at the firm with business in it: State bar membership record No. 48213 shows the license held under that bar number in active suspension, effective March 2000 and continuing, with reinstatement not yet granted.
[knows], one ordinary act of Person A's that the fact explains: The staff attorney, when the paralegal sets up signature pages for the spring filings to the state utility commission, asks by email that a colleague in the department be listed as signing attorney of record on each filing and that the staff attorney's own name appear only on the internal review line.
[concealment], Person A's act toward Person B on the occasion the part gives: The staff attorney tells the general counsel that the attorney was admitted to the state bar in 1993 on the first attempt, has completed this year's continuing legal education hours, paid the annual bar dues in January, and has never had a malpractice claim filed against them.

In this way the threads work as an AND gate: all three together say that Person A keeps this fact from Person B, and any one or two do not, because Person A is not on the [fact] thread and the [knows] thread holds the fact only by its reference. A reader knows everything on a thread they
send, receive, are copied on or are forwarded, quoted parts included.

Use these people, by placeholder:
Person A: the actor, who keeps the secret: an in-house staff attorney in the energy company's legal department; works at the firm.
Person B: the victim, kept from the fact: the general counsel.
Person C: who writes or receives the record; not the person the fact is about; you decide who.
Anyone else the threads need continues the letters from Person D.

## The four pieces

1. The stake: what Person B is about to do, relying on not knowing, that goes wrong because of it.
2. The people: who each placeholder is and whether they work at the firm.
3. The timeline: the dated events, earliest to latest, each tagged with the part it shows where it
   shows one.
4. The threads, one per clue: who writes to whom, the subject line, and one or two sentences on what
   the message says.

Choices, so that chains do not all take one shape. "Use" means use it unless it cannot fit these
people, then choose another and say so in the choices field; "choose" means pick the one that fits,
or write a better one:
- carrier_fact, how [fact] shows up in the mailbox: use: the other person in the fact writing to someone at the firm, not Person A, on business of their own that rests on the fact
- carrier_concealment, the occasion of [concealment]: what brings the matter up between Person A and Person B: use: one message from the actor to the victim, unprompted
- after, what Person B does once Person A has acted: use: makes a plan that depends on it
- naming, how a subject line names the matter, where it does: choose one, or write a better one: a short subject line, like the real ones shown; a file name, like the real ones shown; an account, order or case number; a date
  Real subject lines from this mailbox: Information Regardfing your Tax Returns; Car Registration; KEOL / Credit / GCP Responses 6/8/00; Schedule for Expert Stories; Update - Executive Committee List; real file names: Interim Note.doc, Option to Purchase Real Estate re TitanFehr.DOC, sourcequestions.doc, covs-c.doc. A file name appears only where the people on that thread would use it.

Before you answer, check the answer against these conditions:
- the parts sit as laid out above, and no thread carries both [fact] and [concealment];
- every from and to is a placeholder, and someone at the firm is on every message;
- every message is dated on an event of the timeline, and every date is in 2001;
- the [fact] thread names whom it concerns by the reference only, not Person A, Person B or Person A's
  household, and Person A is not on it;
- the [knows] thread carries the record's reference, in its tie field and in a message, and says in
  Person A's words whom or what it belongs to;
- the [concealment] thread carries neither the record's reference nor its particulars, and names the
  matter as an outsider would;
- Where Person B asks, the question names the matter no more closely than an outsider would.

Ms. Lorah,

We received the January payment your office submitted on behalf of Member No. 48213. We are unable to post it as active annual dues for 2001. Our records show that the license under that bar number has been in active suspension since March 2000, and reinstatement has not been granted.

Please let us know how you would like us to handle the payment. We can issue a refund to your office, or we can hold the funds and apply them toward a reinstatement fee.

Sincerely,

Kinleigh Alatalo
Membership Records
State Bar

Thank you for letting us know. Could you send me the refund amount and the date it will be issued? I need both to correct our department's dues ledger.

Thanks,
Celeste

chains.plot_prompt:
# Lay out the story and the email threads

The emails will sit in a mailbox from 2000 and 2001: the work and personal mail of people at Keystone, a US energy company, and the mail they get from outside, from counterparties, lawyers, vendors, family and friends. Every email in it is sent or received by someone at the firm. The firm, the people and every address in it are invented.

We are hiding one secret in this mailbox, spread over three email threads. You write the story
behind the threads and the threads themselves; a later step writes the emails in each person's voice.

The secret: The staff attorney's law license is suspended, and the attorney keeps this from the general counsel while going on reviewing contracts and advising on regulatory filings as a lawyer.
How it is kept: lying by omission: the actor writes to the victim where the fact belonged and leaves it out.
Kind of secret: dark secret, a fact about the actor themself that does not fit who they are taken to be. The case sits in the actor's work at the firm.

The secret is split into three parts, and each thread carries one:
[fact], the truth as a record holds it, written by someone other than Person A to someone at the firm with business in it: State bar disciplinary order No. 00-DB-0417 suspends the holder of attorney registration No. 208133 from the practice of law for six months, effective October 1, 2000, with reinstatement conditioned on a further petition to the bar.
[knows], one ordinary act of Person A's that the fact explains: The staff attorney, as the legal department's paralegal prepares the signature pages for the quarterly regulatory rate filing due at the federal commission, asks the paralegal by email to list the outside firm's associate as counsel of record and to leave the staff attorney's own bar number off the signature block.
[concealment], Person A's act toward Person B on the occasion the part gives: The staff attorney, answering the general counsel's year-end memo asking every lawyer in the department to confirm their bar admissions and standing for the company's professional liability insurance renewal, returns the completed questionnaire listing the state of admission, the year admitted, and the continuing legal education hours logged, and is silent on the suspension of the staff attorney's license.

In this way the threads work as an AND gate: all three together say that Person A keeps this fact from Person B, and any one or two do not, because Person A is not on the [fact] thread and the [knows] thread holds the fact only by its reference. A reader knows everything on a thread they
send, receive, are copied on or are forwarded, quoted parts included.

Use these people, by placeholder:
Person A: the actor, who keeps the secret: an in-house staff attorney in the energy company's legal department; works at the firm.
Person B: the victim, kept from the fact: the general counsel.
Person C: who writes or receives the record; not the person the fact is about; you decide who.
Anyone else the threads need continues the letters from Person D.

## The four pieces

1. The stake: what Person B is about to do, relying on not knowing, that goes wrong because of it.
2. The people: who each placeholder is and whether they work at the firm.
3. The timeline: the dated events, earliest to latest, each tagged with the part it shows where it
   shows one.
4. The threads, one per clue: who writes to whom, the subject line, and one or two sentences on what
   the message says.

Choices, so that chains do not all take one shape. "Use" means use it unless it cannot fit these
people, then choose another and say so in the choices field; "choose" means pick the one that fits,
or write a better one:
- carrier_fact, how [fact] shows up in the mailbox: choose one, or write a better one: a record from outside the firm, a notice, statement, report or letter, sent to the office at the firm whose business it is: payroll, benefits, travel, expenses, security, a manager; the other person in the fact writing to someone at the firm, not Person A, on business of their own that rests on the fact; an event with consequences that reach an office at the firm: an unpaid invoice, a cancelled booking, a refused renewal, a query from a bank, an agency or a court
- the occasion of [concealment] is the one the part names; keep it
- after, what Person B does once Person A has acted: choose one, or write a better one: commits money or signs; passes it on to someone else as settled; makes a plan that depends on it; lets a deadline pass; drops a check they would otherwise have made; replies with thanks and nothing more
- naming, how a subject line names the matter, where it does: choose one, or write a better one: a short subject line, like the real ones shown; a file name, like the real ones shown; an account, order or case number; a date
  Real subject lines from this mailbox: EDI Training; ENN - New Issue; Closing document re Napoleonville land conveyance; RTP project; New lease option; real file names: PCB Graphs.xls, Experiencing God Week 5.doc, URG Cost Recovery and Balancing Account Leg.doc, Megslops.doc. A file name appears only where the people on that thread would use it.

Before you answer, check the answer against these conditions:
- the parts sit as laid out above, and no thread carries both [fact] and [concealment];
- every from and to is a placeholder, and someone at the firm is on every message;
- every message is dated on an event of the timeline, and every date is in 2001;
- the [fact] thread names whom it concerns by the reference only, not Person A, Person B or Person A's
  household, and Person A is not on it;
- the [knows] thread carries the record's reference, in its tie field and in a message, and says in
  Person A's words whom or what it belongs to;
- the [concealment] thread carries neither the record's reference nor its particulars, and names the
  matter as an outsider would;
- Person B asks what the part says they ask, naming the matter no more closely than an outsider would; Person A's message does what it is for, with no denial, reassurance or status. Where the fact is a standing arrangement between Person A and someone else, an affair, a side arrangement, a second household: Person A's thread with that person and Person A's thread with Person B run through the same weeks and touch the same days, money or place, and neither names the other.

Answer with one JSON object; each field holds its value and nothing else:
{"stake": "what the victim is about to do, one clause",
 "people": [{"person": "Person ?", "function": "what this person is in the secret, as listed above, or other", "role": "who this person is, in a few words", "at_firm": "yes or no"}],
 "timeline": [{"date": "YYYY-MM-DD", "event": "one clause", "shows": "the part this event shows, or empty"}],

chains.plot_prompt:
# Lay out the story and the email threads

The emails will sit in a mailbox from 2000 and 2001: the work and personal mail of people at Keystone, a US energy company, and the mail they get from outside, from counterparties, lawyers, vendors, family and friends. Every email in it is sent or received by someone at the firm. The firm, the people and every address in it are invented.

We are hiding one secret in this mailbox, spread over three email threads. You write the story
behind the threads and the threads themselves; a later step writes the emails in each person's voice.

The secret: A married woman has decided to divorce her husband and has a lawyer preparing the filing, and she keeps this from him while carrying on at home as usual.
How it is kept: lying by commission: the actor tells the victim something about the matter that is false.
Kind of secret: strategic secret, a decision or preparation of the actor's or their group's, kept from the people it lands on until it is done. The case sits in the actor's life outside work; the job is not part of it.

The secret is split into three parts, and each thread carries one:
[fact], the truth as a record holds it, written by someone other than Person A to someone at the firm with business in it: Case file DR-2001-0417 holds a draft petition for dissolution of marriage, prepared by retained counsel and set to be filed on March 12, 2001.
[knows], one ordinary act of Person A's that the fact explains: The wife, on renewing her car insurance in February, writes to the insurance agent asking that the new policy be issued in her name alone, starting in April.
[concealment], Person A's act toward Person B on the occasion the part gives: The wife tells her husband that she has no intention of ending their marriage.

In this way the threads work as an AND gate: all three together say that Person A keeps this fact from Person B, and any one or two do not, because Person A is not on the [fact] thread and the [knows] thread holds the fact only by its reference. A reader knows everything on a thread they
send, receive, are copied on or are forwarded, quoted parts included.

Use these people, by placeholder:
Person A: the actor, who keeps the secret: a married woman planning divorce; works at the firm, in a job you choose to fit the case.
Person B: the victim, kept from the fact: her husband.
Person C: who writes or receives the record; not the person the fact is about; you decide who.
Anyone else the threads need continues the letters from Person D.

## The four pieces

1. The stake: what Person B is about to do, relying on not knowing, that goes wrong because of it.
2. The people: who each placeholder is and whether they work at the firm.
3. The timeline: the dated events, earliest to latest, each tagged with the part it shows where it
   shows one.
4. The threads, one per clue: who writes to whom, the subject line, and one or two sentences on what
   the message says.

Choices, so that chains do not all take one shape. "Use" means use it unless it cannot fit these
people, then choose another and say so in the choices field; "choose" means pick the one that fits,
or write a better one:
- carrier_fact, how [fact] shows up in the mailbox: choose one, or write a better one: a record from outside the firm, a notice, statement, report or letter, sent to the office at the firm whose business it is: payroll, benefits, travel, expenses, security, a manager; the other person in the fact writing to someone at the firm, not Person A, on business of their own that rests on the fact
- carrier_concealment, the occasion of [concealment]: what brings the matter up between Person A and Person B: choose one, or write a better one: one message from the actor to the victim, unprompted; the actor's reply to a direct question the victim asked; the actor's answer inside a thread the victim started about something else; an action the victim relies on: the actor signs, books, approves or sends something
- after, what Person B does once Person A has acted: choose one, or write a better one: commits money or signs; passes it on to someone else as settled; makes a plan that depends on it; lets a deadline pass; drops a check they would otherwise have made; replies with thanks and nothing more
- naming, how a subject line names the matter, where it does: choose one, or write a better one: a short subject line, like the real ones shown; a file name, like the real ones shown; an account, order or case number; a date
  Real subject lines from this mailbox: Roswell Station Remediation - Recovery System; Innovative Tax Strategies developed for the executive; Environmental Strategy Meeting; Update on Gaza Project Developments; Gift Certificate; real file names: Boston Risk Conference Agenda.doc, Invite.doc, PCB Graphs.xls, COMM SubDoc.doc. A file name appears only where the people on that thread would use it.

Before you answer, check the answer against these conditions:
- the parts sit as laid out above, and no thread carries both [fact] and [concealment];
- every from and to is a placeholder, and someone at the firm is on every message;
- every message is dated on an event of the timeline, and every date is in 2001;
- the [fact] thread names whom it concerns by the reference only, not Person A, Person B or Person A's
  household, and Person A is not on it;
- the [knows] thread carries the record's reference, in its tie field and in a message, and says in
  Person A's words whom or what it belongs to;
- the [concealment] thread carries neither the record's reference nor its particulars, and names the
  matter as an outsider would;
- A decision not yet announced is held as the decision and its preparation, with nothing about who has been told. The record names the site it concerns by a reference, as it would a person; the site's name sits in the [knows] thread.

messages.subject: DR-2001-0417
messages.body:
Savion,

A quick update on case file DR-2001-0417. The draft petition for dissolution of marriage has been prepared under the retainer and is in the file. We have filing scheduled for March 12, 2001.

Before then I will need the filing-cost advance you agreed to cover. Please send it at your earliest convenience. A check made out to the firm is fine. Call me if you need the exact figure again or have any questions.

Thanks,

Lenora Abuzahra

messages.body:
Tamiko,

DR-2001-0417 is my file. When you renew my car insurance, please issue the new policy in my name alone starting April 1.

Let me know if you need anything else from me to get it done.

Thanks, Rosann

messages.subject: Kitchen deposit
messages.body:
Ro,

The contractor wants the deposit this week to hold our spot. It's nonrefundable and it would come out of our savings. Before I write the check I have to ask you straight out, because things have felt off lately: are you thinking about ending our marriage? If you are, I'd rather know now than after the money's gone.

Rogan

messages.subject: RE: Kitchen deposit
messages.body:
No, I have no intention of ending our marriage. Go ahead with the kitchen deposit.

Rosann

messages.subject: RE: Kitchen deposit
messages.body:
Done. I paid the deposit out of savings this morning. It's nonrefundable, so we're officially getting a new kitchen.

R.
