chains.plot_prompt:
# Lay out the story and the email threads

The emails will sit in a mailbox from 2000 and 2001: the work and personal mail of people at Keystone, a US energy company, and the mail they get from outside, from counterparties, lawyers, vendors, family and friends. Every email in it is sent or received by someone at the firm. The firm, the people and every address in it are invented.

We are hiding one secret in this mailbox, spread over three email threads. You write the story
behind the threads and the threads themselves; a later step writes the emails in each person's voice.

The secret: A married woman has decided to divorce her husband and has a lawyer preparing the filing, and she keeps this from him while carrying on at home as usual.
How it is kept: paltering: the actor gives the victim true statements about the matter, chosen so that the victim takes away a false picture of it; nothing said is false, and the fact is neither stated nor denied.
Kind of secret: strategic secret, a decision or preparation of the actor's or their group's, kept from the people it lands on until it is done. The case sits in the actor's life outside work; the job is not part of it.

The secret is split into three parts, and each thread carries one:
[fact], the truth as a record holds it, written by someone other than Person A to someone at the firm with business in it: Family law matter no. 01-DR-0417 holds a drafted petition for dissolution of marriage, with the retainer paid and the petition awaiting signature and filing.
[knows], one ordinary act of Person A's that the fact explains: The wife, when her car insurance comes up for its spring renewal, writes to the insurance agent asking that at the next term the policy be reissued in her name alone with a separate billing address.
[concealment], Person A's act toward Person B on the occasion the part gives: The wife tells her husband that the attorney she has been meeting with is helping her get her own papers in order, including an updated will, that the late evenings are because things have been busy, and that she has already paid the deposit on the August lake cabin as she does every year.

In this way the threads work as an AND gate: all three together say that Person A keeps this fact from Person B, and any one or two do not, because Person A is not on the [fact] thread and the [knows] thread holds the fact only by its reference. A reader knows everything on a thread they
send, receive, are copied on or are forwarded, quoted parts included.

Use these people, by placeholder:
Person A: the actor, who keeps the secret: a married woman planning divorce; works at the firm, in a job you choose to fit the case.
Person B: the victim, kept from the fact: her husband.
Person C: who writes or receives the record; not the person the fact is about; you decide who.
Anyone else the threads need continues the letters from Person D.

## The four pieces

1. The stake: what Person B is about to do, relying on not knowing, that goes wrong because of it.
2. The people: who each placeholder is and whether they work at the firm.
3. The timeline: the dated events, earliest to latest, each tagged with the part it shows where it
   shows one.
4. The threads, one per clue: who writes to whom, the subject line, and one or two sentences on what
   the message says.

Choices, so that chains do not all take one shape. "Use" means use it unless it cannot fit these
people, then choose another and say so in the choices field; "choose" means pick the one that fits,
or write a better one:
- carrier_fact, how [fact] shows up in the mailbox: choose one, or write a better one: a record from outside the firm, a notice, statement, report or letter, sent to the office at the firm whose business it is: payroll, benefits, travel, expenses, security, a manager; the other person in the fact writing to someone at the firm, not Person A, on business of their own that rests on the fact
- carrier_concealment, the occasion of [concealment]: what brings the matter up between Person A and Person B: choose one, or write a better one: one message from the actor to the victim, unprompted; a report, status or handoff the actor sends the victim, unprompted; the actor's reply to a direct question the victim asked; the actor's answer inside a thread the victim started about something else; an action the victim relies on: the actor signs, books, approves or sends something, with a true note on it
- after, what Person B does once Person A has acted: choose one, or write a better one: commits money or signs; passes it on to someone else as settled; makes a plan that depends on it; lets a deadline pass; drops a check they would otherwise have made; replies with thanks and nothing more
- naming, how a subject line names the matter, where it does: choose one, or write a better one: a short subject line, like the real ones shown; a file name, like the real ones shown; an account, order or case number; a date
  Real subject lines from this mailbox: Conference Call; Vacation Time; Application for Admission; Yasmin's Direct Testimony - Comprehensive Settlement Agreement; Ces lease/USTELENET DMS; real file names: SB 27xx - mockup.doc, registration form.doc, PCB Graphs.xls, PMW conference.pdf. A file name appears only where the people on that thread would use it.

Before you answer, check the answer against these conditions:
- the parts sit as laid out above, and no thread carries both [fact] and [concealment];
- every from and to is a placeholder, and someone at the firm is on every message;
- every message is dated on an event of the timeline, and every date is in 2001;
- the [fact] thread names whom it concerns by the reference only, not Person A, Person B or Person A's
  household, and Person A is not on it;
- the [knows] thread carries the record's reference, in its tie field and in a message, and says in
  Person A's words whom or what it belongs to;
- the [concealment] thread carries neither the record's reference nor its particulars, and names the
  matter as an outsider would;
- A decision not yet announced is held as the decision and its preparation, with nothing about who has been told. The record names the site it concerns by a reference, as it would a person; the site's name sits in the [knows] thread.
- Where Person B asks, the question names the matter no more closely than an outsider would.

Answer with one JSON object; each field holds its value and nothing else:

 "people": [{"person": "Person ?", "function": "what this person is in the secret, as listed above, or other", "role": "who this person is, in a few words", "at_firm": "yes or no"}],

Rosann

Antwain

# Lay out the story and the email threads

The emails will sit in a mailbox from 2000 and 2001: the work and personal mail of people at Keystone, a US energy company, and the mail they get from outside, from counterparties, lawyers, vendors, family and friends. How it is kept: lying by omission: the actor writes to the victim where the fact belonged and leaves it out.
Kind of secret: strategic secret, a decision or preparation of the actor's or their group's, kept from the people it lands on until it is done. The case sits in the actor's life outside work; the job is not part of it.

The secret is split into three parts, and each thread carries one:
[fact], the truth as a record holds it, written by someone other than Person A to someone at the firm with business in it: File D-417 records a decision to end a marriage and a lawyer’s preparation of a divorce filing.
[knows], one ordinary act of Person A's that the fact explains: The married woman, while scheduling an appointment under file D-417, emails the lawyer’s assistant to request a Tuesday morning slot.
[concealment], Person A's act toward Person B on the occasion the part gives: The married woman, when her husband asks in writing about their plans for the coming month, replies with the dates of family errands and is silent on her decision about their marriage.

In this way the threads work as an AND gate: all three together say that Person A keeps this fact from Person B, and any one or two do not, because Person A is not on the [fact] thread and the [knows] thread holds the fact only by its reference. A reader knows everything on a thread they
send, receive, are copied on or are forwarded, quoted parts included.

Use these people, by placeholder:
Person A: the actor, who keeps the secret: a married woman planning divorce; works at the firm, in a job you choose to fit the case.
Person B: the victim, kept from the fact: the husband.
Person C: who writes or receives the record; not the person the fact is about; you decide who.
Anyone else the threads need continues the letters from Person D.

## The four pieces

1. The stake: what Person B is about to do, relying on not knowing, that goes wrong because of it.
2. The people: who each placeholder is and whether they work at the firm.
3. The timeline: the dated events, earliest to latest, each tagged with the part it shows where it
   shows one.
4. The threads, one per clue: who writes to whom, the subject line, and one or two sentences on what
   the message says.

people, then choose another and say so in the choices field; "choose" means pick the one that fits,

- the occasion of [concealment] is the one the part names; keep it
- after, what Person B does once Person A has acted: choose one, or write a better one: commits money or signs; passes it on to someone else as settled; makes a plan that depends on it; lets a deadline pass; drops a check they would otherwise have made; replies with thanks and nothing more

messages.body:
Kalyn,

Following up on the guarantor review you requested last week. The supplemental record came back this morning and shows one revolving item of note:

Card account ending 4417
Balance: $23,800 (at credit limit)
Minimum payment missed in 3 of the last 4 billing cycles

The full report will follow by fax. Let me know if you need the tradeline detail pulled separately.

Regards,

Tyrel Alesci
Commercial Services
555-613-2280

messages.subject: Rehearsal dinner
messages.body:
Hi Iona,

Just confirming the quote we went over on the phone: the rehearsal dinner for 42 guests, plated with the salmon and chicken options, wine service and dessert, comes to $3,150 including tax and gratuity.

As you asked, I've split it into two invoices, one half to you and one half to the groom's side, charged to the card ending 4417 that was given to us. Let me know if anything needs to change before I send them out.

Thanks so much,
Lexis Abughannam
555-307-4461

messages.subject: Re: Rehearsal dinner
messages.body:
Lexis,

Please make the full invoice out to me alone and don't split it. The card ending 4417 that was proposed for the groom's share belongs to my brother. I'll send you my card information today.

Thanks,
Iona

messages.subject: Apartment lease
messages.body:
Iona,

This feels a little awkward to ask, but you're the only one I trust to give me a straight answer. We're supposed to sign the lease on the new apartment Monday, both our names on it. Before I do, does he have any debts I should know about? He always changes the subject when I bring up money.

Love,
Cherri

messages.subject: Re: Apartment lease
messages.body:
Cherri,

He owes nothing to anyone beyond the last few payments on his car.

Iona

messages.subject: Re: Apartment lease
messages.body:
Thank you, that was a big relief. We signed the joint lease this morning! You'll have to come see the place once we're moved in.

Cherri

chains.plot_prompt:
# Lay out the story and the email threads

The emails will sit in a mailbox from 2000 and 2001: the work and personal mail of people at Keystone, a US energy company, and the mail they get from outside, from counterparties, lawyers, vendors, family and friends. Every email in it is sent or received by someone at the firm. The firm, the people and every address in it are invented.

We are hiding one secret in this mailbox, spread over three email threads. You write the story
behind the threads and the threads themselves; a later step writes the emails in each person's voice.

The secret: She keeps it to herself that her brother is deep in credit card debt he cannot pay down.
How it is kept: paltering: the actor gives the victim true statements about the matter, chosen so that the victim takes away a false picture of it; nothing said is false, and the fact is neither stated nor denied.
Kind of secret: entrusted secret, a fact about someone else that the actor holds because of what the actor is to the person the fact is about. The case sits in the actor's life outside work; the job is not part of it.

The secret is split into three parts, and each thread carries one:
[fact], the truth as a record holds it, written by someone other than Person A to someone at the firm with business in it: Revolving credit account ref. 4417-CC shows a balance at its credit limit, only minimum payments made for the past eleven cycles, and a hardship request declined in March 2001.
[knows], one ordinary act of Person A's that the fact explains: The older sister, writing to the caterer to confirm the menu for the rehearsal dinner, asks that the deposit be charged to her own card instead of the groom's, as had first been arranged.
[concealment], Person A's act toward Person B on the occasion the part gives: The older sister tells the brother's fiancée that he has never once been late with his rent, that he paid for all the new furniture in their apartment himself, and that ever since college he has been the one in the family who keeps a budget written down in a notebook.

In this way the threads work as an AND gate: all three together say that Person A keeps this fact from Person B, and any one or two do not, because Person A is not on the [fact] thread and the [knows] thread holds the fact only by its reference. A reader knows everything on a thread they
send, receive, are copied on or are forwarded, quoted parts included.

Use these people, by placeholder:
Person A: the actor, who keeps the secret: a woman, the older sister; works at the firm, in a job you choose to fit the case.
Person B: the victim, kept from the fact: the brother's fiancée.
Person C: who writes or receives the record; not the person the fact is about; you decide who.
Anyone else the threads need continues the letters from Person D.

## The four pieces

1. The stake: what Person B is about to do, relying on not knowing, that goes wrong because of it.
2. The people: who each placeholder is and whether they work at the firm.
3. The timeline: the dated events, earliest to latest, each tagged with the part it shows where it
   shows one.
4. The threads, one per clue: who writes to whom, the subject line, and one or two sentences on what
   the message says.

Choices, so that chains do not all take one shape. "Use" means use it unless it cannot fit these
people, then choose another and say so in the choices field; "choose" means pick the one that fits,
or write a better one:
- carrier_fact, how [fact] shows up in the mailbox: choose one, or write a better one: a record from outside the firm, a notice, statement, report or letter, sent to the office at the firm whose business it is: payroll, benefits, travel, expenses, security, a manager; the other person in the fact writing to someone at the firm, not Person A, on business of their own that rests on the fact
- carrier_concealment, the occasion of [concealment]: what brings the matter up between Person A and Person B: choose one, or write a better one: one message from the actor to the victim, unprompted; a report, status or handoff the actor sends the victim, unprompted; the actor's reply to a direct question the victim asked; the actor's answer inside a thread the victim started about something else; an action the victim relies on: the actor signs, books, approves or sends something, with a true note on it
- after, what Person B does once Person A has acted: choose one, or write a better one: commits money or signs; passes it on to someone else as settled; makes a plan that depends on it; lets a deadline pass; drops a check they would otherwise have made; replies with thanks and nothing more
- naming, how a subject line names the matter, where it does: choose one, or write a better one: a short subject line, like the real ones shown; a file name, like the real ones shown; an account, order or case number; a date
  Real subject lines from this mailbox: Velva's resume; Environmental Strategy Meeting; POWER Conference Sponsorship by Keystone; Sat night - the plan; District Cooling Project - Project Financing; real file names: SB 27xx - mockup.doc, CFTC - CFMA COMMENT LETTER FINAL.doc, Members and Bios.doc, Keystone Art Collection Vision.doc. A file name appears only where the people on that thread would use it.

chains.plot_prompt:
# Lay out the story and the email threads

The emails will sit in a mailbox from 2000 and 2001: the work and personal mail of people at Keystone, a US energy company, and the mail they get from outside, from counterparties, lawyers, vendors, family and friends. Every email in it is sent or received by someone at the firm. The firm, the people and every address in it are invented.

We are hiding one secret in this mailbox, spread over three email threads. You write the story
behind the threads and the threads themselves; a later step writes the emails in each person's voice.

The secret: She keeps it to herself that her brother is deep in credit card debt he cannot pay down.
How it is kept: lying by omission: the actor writes to the victim where the fact belonged and leaves it out.
Kind of secret: entrusted secret, a fact about someone else that the actor holds because of what the actor is to the person the fact is about. The case sits in the actor's life outside work; the job is not part of it.

The secret is split into three parts, and each thread carries one:
[fact], the truth as a record holds it, written by someone other than Person A to someone at the firm with business in it: Wedding budget file W-07 records $24,000 in credit-card debt that its subject cannot pay down on current income.
[knows], one ordinary act of Person A's that the fact explains: The older sister, while arranging the rehearsal dinner for wedding W-07, emails the restaurant to ask whether she can pay the deposit herself.
[concealment], Person A's act toward Person B on the occasion the part gives: The older sister, answering the fiancée’s request for an overview of her future husband’s finances before they set a wedding budget, emails the fiancée his income, rent, and car payment and says nothing about credit-card debt.

In this way the threads work as an AND gate: all three together say that Person A keeps this fact from Person B, and any one or two do not, because Person A is not on the [fact] thread and the [knows] thread holds the fact only by its reference. A reader knows everything on a thread they
send, receive, are copied on or are forwarded, quoted parts included.

Use these people, by placeholder:
Person A: the actor, who keeps the secret: a woman, the older sister; works at the firm, in a job you choose to fit the case.
Person B: the victim, kept from the fact: the fiancée.
Person C: who writes or receives the record; not the person the fact is about; you decide who.
Anyone else the threads need continues the letters from Person D.

## The four pieces

1. The stake: what Person B is about to do, relying on not knowing, that goes wrong because of it.
2. The people: who each placeholder is and whether they work at the firm.
3. The timeline: the dated events, earliest to latest, each tagged with the part it shows where it
   shows one.
4. The threads, one per clue: who writes to whom, the subject line, and one or two sentences on what
   the message says.

Choices, so that chains do not all take one shape. "Use" means use it unless it cannot fit these
people, then choose another and say so in the choices field; "choose" means pick the one that fits,
or write a better one:
- carrier_fact, how [fact] shows up in the mailbox: choose one, or write a better one: a record from outside the firm, a notice, statement, report or letter, sent to the office at the firm whose business it is: payroll, benefits, travel, expenses, security, a manager; the other person in the fact writing to someone at the firm, not Person A, on business of their own that rests on the fact
- the occasion of [concealment] is the one the part names; keep it
- after, what Person B does once Person A has acted: choose one, or write a better one: commits money or signs; passes it on to someone else as settled; makes a plan that depends on it; lets a deadline pass; drops a check they would otherwise have made; replies with thanks and nothing more
- naming, how a subject line names the matter, where it does: choose one, or write a better one: a short subject line, like the real ones shown; a file name, like the real ones shown; an account, order or case number; a date
  Real subject lines from this mailbox: ETC - Community Service Project; POWER Conference Sponsorship by Keystone; ISO Filing; Spa Schedule; New lease option; real file names: REVISED Merged Leg Language.doc, Megslops.doc, CFTC - CFMA COMMENT LETTER FINAL.doc, GasTurbi.DOC. A file name appears only where the people on that thread would use it.

Before you answer, check the answer against these conditions:
- the parts sit as laid out above, and no thread carries both [fact] and [concealment];
- every from and to is a placeholder, and someone at the firm is on every message;
- every message is dated on an event of the timeline, and every date is in 2001;
- the [fact] thread names whom it concerns by the reference only, not Person A, Person B or Person A's
  household, and Person A is not on it;
- the [knows] thread carries the record's reference, in its tie field and in a message, and says in
  Person A's words whom or what it belongs to;
- the [concealment] thread carries neither the record's reference nor its particulars, and names the
  matter as an outsider would;
- Person B asks what the part says they ask, naming the matter no more closely than an outsider would; Person A's message does what it is for, with no denial, reassurance or status. Where the fact is a standing arrangement between Person A and someone else, an affair, a side arrangement, a second household: Person A's thread with that person and Person A's thread with Person B run through the same weeks and touch the same days, money or place, and neither names the other.

Answer with one JSON object; each field holds its value and nothing else:
{"stake": "what the victim is about to do, one clause",
 "people": [{"person": "Person ?", "function": "what this person is in the secret, as listed above, or other", "role": "who this person is, in a few words", "at_firm": "yes or no"}],
 "timeline": [{"date": "YYYY-MM-DD", "event": "one clause", "shows": "the part this event shows, or empty"}],
 "choices": {"carrier_fact": "the option used, in its first words", "after": "the option used, in its first words", "naming": "the option used, in its first words"},
 "clues": [{"i": 1, "carries": ["fact"], "reference": "the name this thread uses for the matter, or empty", "tie": "the record's reference as the [knows] thread carries it; empty for other clues", "line": "Person A's message to Person B, in substance: what it says and nothing of what it leaves out; empty for other clues",
            "messages": [{"from": "Person ?", "to": ["Person ?"], "date": "YYYY-MM-DD", "subject": "...", "what_happens": "what the message says, one or two sentences, nothing of what its reader makes of it"}]}]}

plot_checks: read: clue 2: the [knows] thread adds words of the fact beyond its part: budge

messages.subject: W-07
messages.body:
Savion,

Thanks again for giving us your Saturdays. I have one more file for you when you get a minute. W-07 is a wedding budget that came in last week. The worksheet shows $24,000 in credit-card debt, and as far as I can tell there is no way to pay it down on the current income. The subject is still planning the wedding on top of it.

Could you check the arithmetic for the clinic before we sit down with them? I'd hate to tell someone the numbers don't work if I've added something up wrong. The file is in the blue folder at the front desk, or I can fax the pages to you.

Thanks,
Geoffrey
Clinic Coordinator

messages.subject: Rehearsal dinner
messages.body:
Mr. Anguino,

I'm writing about the rehearsal dinner booked for the end of May. W-07 is my brother's wedding budget, and I would rather the dinner not come out of it. Can I pay the rehearsal-dinner deposit myself? If so, please let me know the amount and whether you take a personal check or need a card over the phone.

Thank you,
Rosann Polosky
3-4417

messages.subject: Wedding budget
messages.body:
Hi Rosann,

We're finally sitting down to set the wedding budget this week and I'd like to get it right the first time. Your brother is sweet but hopeless with numbers, and every time I ask he says "it's fine, don't worry about it." Could you give me a rough overview of his finances? Just the basics, so I know what we can actually spend.

Thanks so much. I owe you one!

Tayla

messages.subject: Re: Wedding budget
messages.body:
Tayla,

He makes $41,000 a year. His rent is $850 a month and his car payment is $315 a month.

Rosann

messages.subject: Re: Wedding budget
messages.body:
Thank you!! I used your figures to set the budget and it all came out fine. I signed the venue contract this morning. Can't wait to show you the place!

T.
